title: Dynamic Credit Scoring for Financial Inclusion: Evaluating Machine Learning Methods in the Zambian Credit Market
tldr: Random Forest outperforms Logistic Regression in dynamic credit scoring for Zambian informal financial institutions, promoting financial inclusion.
problem_and_motivation: Financial institutions heavily rely on credit scoring for informed lending decisions. In Zambia, limited research exists on applying ML methods for credit scoring, particularly for informal financial institutions. The goal is to develop a more inclusive credit scoring system that can serve individuals without formal banking history, thereby promoting financial inclusion in the Zambian context.
approach: Collected credit data from 500 customers of a Zambian SACCO (Savings and Credit Cooperative).
Built ML models using Random Forest (RF) and Logistic Regression (LR) algorithms.
Tested multiple hyperparameter configurations: RF with n=100, n=200, n=300 trees and m=4,8,10,12 split features; LR with C=0.1,0.5,1 regularization.
Used 80/20 train/test split with stratified sampling.
Compared model performance using AUC, precision, recall, and F1-score metrics.
Implemented dynamic credit scoring with periodic retraining to address concept drift.
findings: Random Forest significantly outperforms Logistic Regression for credit scoring in the Zambian context.
Best RF model (m=8, n=200) achieved AUC=0.988, precision=0.956, recall=0.931, F1=0.943.
Best LR model (C=0.1) achieved AUC=0.949, precision=0.862, recall=0.877, F1=0.869.
Random Forest's higher performance is attributed to its ability to capture non-linear relationships in credit data.
Dynamic credit scoring with periodic retraining addresses temporal changes in credit behavior patterns.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: This paper demonstrates that Random Forest significantly outperforms Logistic Regression for credit scoring in the Zambian informal financial sector (SACCOs). It addresses the gap in applying ML credit scoring in developing economies where many individuals lack formal banking history. The dynamic credit scoring approach with periodic retraining addresses concept drift, ensuring models remain accurate as borrower behavior changes over time. The work promotes financial inclusion by enabling informal financial institutions to make data-driven lending decisions.
directly_justifies: Random Forest achieves AUC=0.988 compared to Logistic Regression's AUC=0.949.
Dynamic credit scoring with periodic retraining addresses temporal changes in credit behavior.
ML methods can serve individuals without formal banking history, promoting financial inclusion.
Feature engineering from transaction data is critical for model performance in low-data contexts.
